question: What do Circles v2, Grassroots Economics Sarafu and Cosmo-Local Credit, Kolektivo and GoodDollar do at contract level, at what scale, and what does the evaluation literature report?

frame.exposure: contract source, chain reads, project statistics, peer-reviewed evaluations
frame.comparator: Tidepool member credit lines and pooled credit

item.title: aboutcircles/circles-contracts-v2: Hub, Circles, Demurrage, groups, treasury

findings.finding: Personal currency: every registered human can call personalMint() and claim issuance of one Circle per hour, retroactive for up to 14 days; balances are ERC-1155 token ids equal to the avatar address, with ERC-20 wrappers in two flavours (demurraged and inflationary).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Each individual can mint their own currency at a rate of one Circle per hour.

findings.finding: Demurrage is a decay factor applied per day: GAMMA = 0.93^(1/365.25) in 64.64 fixed point (18443079296116538654), i.e. 7 percent a year; issuance is also expressed in the inflationary frame so that a holder's balance decays while new issuance keeps total supply at an equilibrium.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: To obtain GAMMA for a daily accounting of 7% p.a. demurrage => GAMMA = (0.93)^(1/365.25)

findings.finding: Trust is directed, with an expiry: trust(address _trustReceiver, uint96 _expiry) lets an avatar declare whose personal currency it accepts. Payment is path-based: operateFlowMatrix moves value along a path of trust edges, each hop converting between personal currencies the receiver trusts. The latest CHANGELOG adds consented flow with bidirectional trust and an opt-out to the v1 unidirectional model.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: [PR141] consented flow with bi-directional trust, with opt-out to v1 protocol of uni-directional trust

findings.finding: Registration: registerHuman(inviter) requires the inviter to be a registered human who has trusted the newcomer; after the invitation-only period the inviter burns INVITATION_COST = 96 CRC (2 x WELCOME_BONUS) and the newcomer receives WELCOME_BONUS = 48 CRC. Humans stop() to end their own minting irreversibly.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 private constant WELCOME_BONUS = 48 * EXA; uint256 private constant INVITATION_COST = 2 * WELCOME_BONUS;

findings.finding: Groups: registerGroup(mint policy, name, symbol) creates a group currency; groupMint(group, collateralAvatars, amounts) lets anyone post trusted personal or group Circles as collateral to mint group Circles under the group's mint-policy contract (beforeMintPolicy, beforeBurnPolicy, beforeRedeemPolicy). The default MintPolicy returns true for everything; real constraints live in the policy a group chooses. A StandardTreasury holds the collateral.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: function groupMint(address _group, address[] calldata _collateralAvatars, uint256[] calldata _amounts, bytes calldata _data)

findings.finding: Review reports in repo: reviews/202407-gnosis and reviews/202409-hats. The README calls the repository beta; last commit in the shallow clone 2026-03-05, repository push 2026-05-06; organisation repos pushed in 2026 include group-tms (maintains the trust relations of a group by conditions), trust-score, CirclesMiniapps, marketplace-api, circles-explorer, circlesubi-simulation.

item.title: cosmo-local-credit/protocol: SPEC.md and README deployments (Gnosis, v1.0.0)

findings.finding: Contract set: GiftableToken (ERC-20 voucher with mintTo by owner or writer, optional expiry, burn), SwapPool (AMM without LP tokens: deposit adds liquidity; withdraw(tokenOut, tokenIn, value) is a swap), Limiter (per token and per holder balance caps; 0 blocks deposits), RelativeQuoter (per-token PPM price index), OracleQuoter (Chainlink feeds, multiplier 0.9 to 1.0), DecimalQuoter, FeePolicy (default and per-pair fee in PPM), ProtocolFeeController, Splitter, SwapRouter (multi-hop), EthFaucet, PeriodSimple, CAT, TokenUniqueSymbolIndex, ContractRegistry, AccountsIndex, RescueVault.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Technical reference for every Sarafu Network Protocol smart contract.

findings.finding: Swap mechanics: tokenIn is deposited; quote = quoter.valueFor(out, in, received); pool fee = quote * feePpm / 1,000,000; protocol fee = max(poolFee, 1 percent floor) * protocolFeePpm / PPM; recipient gets quote minus both fees. The floor stops a pool operator setting a tiny pool fee to shrink the protocol's cut. Pools with feesDecoupled keep accrued fees out of swap liquidity.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The floor stops a pool operator from setting a tiny pool fee just to shrink the protocol's cut.

findings.finding: Pool owner can seal configuration bit by bit (fee policy, fee address, quoter, token registry, limiter; maxSealState 31), irreversibly; owner has withdrawLiquidity as an emergency exit; the spec says to use a timelock or multisig owner. Proxied contracts are ERC1967 with the proxy admin required to differ from owner in ge-publish.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Seal is only a commitment when the ERC1967 proxy admin is a different, more conservative principal than the owner

findings.finding: Gnosis mainnet (chain id 100) v1.0.0 implementations: SwapPool 0x9e694D342Cab02e295262B2290b0E64A0334160D, GiftableToken 0x34445d13F112A11f72C1d353a7dcdc407F3df2d8, Limiter 0x258AAd6c933F70D7F071E112800a41Fb60434048, RelativeQuoter 0x0B0986c0E580377389337C453Cc65A3933511165, OracleQuoter 0x3334fd1eA4c7e4dCA51f5E62EE3F5f7Dcbd098BA, FeePolicy 0x1b97FfFAF2D2e16C8F7de6826F4F658dc898E5b6, ProtocolFeeController 0x302E6d520e7D7AeFceA4813e456234B5daA23B4d, SwapRouter 0x16e3F29dDe22eF75C081A764C4d200Cd48647bcC, Splitter 0x3b1F9bCC82f2dA5607dcDFCb21E47Cf64Ee54274, RescueVault 0x3E5D8d8f63c57EA5DD62cF5aeC7212C50bDA69EF; compiler solc 0.8.36, EVM osaka.

Audit: audits/Sarafu-Protocol-Security-Audit.pdf is described in the README as an "Internal engineering review of all protocol contracts at commit f0944d9; this is not an independent third-party certification."

item.title: Cosmo-Local Credit docs and Grassroots Economics documentation

findings.finding: Vouchers are gift-card-like claims on the issuer's goods or services; a Commitment Pool is "a curated place to exchange selected vouchers", with a Pool Steward who chooses supported vouchers and publishes rules, limits and fees. Built and maintained by the Grassroots Economics Foundation, a Kenyan nonprofit working on community exchange tools since 2010.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: A Commitment Pool is a curated place to exchange selected vouchers.

findings.finding: Historical Sarafu Network activity from 2023-07-05 to 2025-07-20: 745 unique active vouchers, 188 unique active Commitment Pools, 26,367 users, 285,197 exchanges between users.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Unique active vouchers: 745 / Unique active Commitment Pools: 188 / Users: 26,367 / Exchanges between users: 285,197

findings.finding: docs.grassecon.org (last update 2026-09-30) defines commitment pooling as "A protocol and practice for routing promises, settlement, and mutual support through shared pools" and states "The service formerly presented as Sarafu Network transitioned to Cosmo-Local Credit", adding that not every historical Sarafu account, token or balance carried over.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The service formerly presented as Sarafu Network transitioned to Cosmo-Local Credit.

notFound: chain and contract addresses in the docs pages read (they point to /protocol/overview, not read)

findings.finding: erc20-pool README: "A token pool implementation that allows deposits in the form of liquidity donations, and withdrawals in the form of token swaps." Table: alice deposit(FOO, 1000000); bob withdraw(FOO, BAR, 1000) gives bob 1000 FOO and takes 1000 BAR from him, the pool moves the other way. Token registry (ACL) controls which tokens are allowed; token limiter caps value per token; a quoter sets price (DecimalQuote converts only decimals).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: A token pool implementation that allows deposits in the form of liquidity donations, and withdrawals in the form of token swaps.

findings.finding: The README warns the pool does no sanity checking of exchange value: "It is therefore the responsibility of the maintainer of the list of allowed tokens to ensure that tokens in the pool are exchangeable in a sensible way", listing different units of account, different value relative to the unit, and different rates of change.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The pool contract does no checking whatsoever regarding the sanity of allowing tokens in the pool.

findings.finding: erc20-demurrage-token: "Everyone is taxed a little something every minute, and every so often a decision is made on how to redistribute that tax"; continuous per-minute decay of balances, a demurrage period after which the decayed value can be withdrawn to a sink account, minting and burning by role, voucher expiration and supply cap changeable after publishing.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Everyone is taxed a little something every minute, and every so often a decision is made on how to redistribute that tax.

item.title: The Kolektivo Framework Whitepaper v.3 (Decentralized Exchange Trading Systems)

findings.finding: Framework on Celo: a decentralized exchange trading system (DETS) issues an elastic-supply community currency (CC) and a reserve token, kCUR for the Curacao pilot, in a collateralized relationship mediated by an AMM described as a modified Mento constant-product reserve with a leverage parameter that allows a partially backed reserve.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The DETS may raise external capital by minting and selling its own reserve token, which we refer to as kCUR

findings.finding: Reserve policy: "For their 20,000 user community, Grassroots Economics currently maintains a 25% target collateral ratio and speculates that 5% is possible"; the framework contrasts this with the Curacao guilder being backed by only 19 percent USD reserves and proposes capital controls (time delay, rate limit, per-address ceilings) on reserve exchange flows.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: For their 20,000 user community, Grassroots Economics currently maintains a 25% target collateral ratio and speculates that 5% is possible.

notFound: a deployed kCUR or Curacao currency contract; none was found in the repos read and DeFiLlama has no Kolektivo listing

findings.finding: SPEC.md specifies a Kolektivo Trinidad and Tobago Dollar (KTTD, ERC-20, 18 decimals, OpenZeppelin Ownable and Pausable) whose ownership passes to a Treasury contract; cash-out is limited to merchants listed by a Merkle root; cash-in and cash-out are authorised by EIP-712 signatures from the treasury key. The only Solidity file in contracts/ is Token.sol; last commit 2024-07-26.

kolektivo-docs holds the mobile wallet project charter (scope: store, send and receive the community currency, QR transfers, GeoNFTs and Activity Tokens, Caribbean communities and climate action); last commit 2025-02-04. Kolektivo-Labs/Kolektivo is a Next.js site (last commit 2024-12-22). The Kolektivo dApp repo was built for Celo L1.

notFound: any reserve contract, minted token supply or user count for Kolektivo

findings.finding: UBIScheme: each cycle (cycleLength = 30 days) the scheme withdraws funds and sets dailyUbi from the pool: nextDailyPool = currentBalance / cycleLength, divided among the previous day's claimers; claim() pays the day's entitlement to a whitelisted identity. Eligibility is by Identity contract whitelisting, not by trust.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 nextDailyPool = currentBalance / cycleLength;

findings.finding: Reserve: Ethereum production deployment has GoodMarketMaker/GoodReserveCDai (Bancor-formula bonding curve against cDAI) with ExchangeHelper; the Celo and XDC deployments list MentoReserve, MentoExchangeProvider, MentoExpansionController and MentoBroker, and G$ is a Superfluid Super Token (SuperGoodDollar pure Super Token).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: SuperGoodDollar is implemented as a Pure Super Token - it has no underlying ERC20.

Published dataset: anonymized account information for around 55,000 users and all Sarafu transactions between 2020-01-25 and 2021-06-15, around 300 million Sarafu in total, covering purchases, transfers and participation in savings and lending groups (chamas). One Sarafu is roughly one Kenyan shilling.

item.title: Cooperative behavior in blockchain-based complementary currency networks through time: The Sarafu case study

findings.finding: Analyses cooperative behaviour in Sarafu over time including the COVID-19 crisis; the group account (chama) is the feature that makes group behaviour observable.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Sarafu is a perfect case study for the study of cooperative behavior, as it implements a special type of account, the group account, to support cooperation groups.

item.title: Affordances of Digital and Blockchain-Based Community Currencies: The Case of Sarafu Network in Kenya
item.container-title: International Journal of Community Currency Research

findings.finding: Qualitative case study of the move from paper vouchers (2010) to feature-phone interface (2016) to blockchain (2018), through several migrations to Community Asset Vouchers on Celo since 2023. Blockchain enabled automated holding-tax calculation and a link from vouchers to stablecoins through liquidity-pool contracts; the study finds a trade-off between blockchain benefits and interface complexity.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The unique contributions of blockchain include enabling automation of holding tax calculations and linking the vouchers to the mainstream monetary system via stablecoins facilitated by a series of smart contracts also known as the liquidity pool.

item.title: Complementary currencies and entrepreneurship: Sustaining micro‐entrepreneurs in Kenyan informal settlements

findings.finding: Qualitative study: Sarafu works as an external enabler changing payment systems, supply and demand and pricing, and when integrated with savings groups it provides financial inclusion and collective purpose.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: when integrated with savings groups, they provide financial inclusion and collective purpose, strengthening local business networks.

item.title: Universal basic income on blockchain: the case of circles UBI

findings.finding: Reviews Circles UBI as a case; the Berlin pilot is described as having failed, and the paper concludes UBI alone, on blockchain or not, does not solve the problems its proponents name, proposing open cooperativism as the production model Circles could plug into.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Examining the failure of the Berlin pilot helps us draw substantial conclusions with regard to the implementation of UBI on blockchain.

item.title: Impact of a Blockchain-based Universal Basic Income Pilot: The case of Circles UBI currency
item.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

findings.finding: Circles UBI active in Berlin since October 2021; the Circles Coop that launched it shut down in December 2023; survey of 25 individuals found participation motivated by identification with community values; first qualitative study of a UBI designed as a community currency on a blockchain.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The Circles Coop, which launched the project in 2021, was shut down in December 2023.

sources.population: 25 survey respondents in the Berlin Circles network, October to November 2023

item.title: Universal Basic Income in a Blockchain-Based Community Currency

findings.finding: Temporal network analysis of the Berlin pilot including a subsidy programme for local businesses: the pilot sustained expansion of the economic network and facilitated trade in urban communities; sustainability of self-organised UBI-issuing currencies and decentralisation of governance are left open.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Our findings suggest that the pilot project sustained the expansion of the economic network and the system facilitated trade in urban communities in Berlin.

sources.population: Circles UBI users in the Berlin pilot
